key_terms.الْفَلَاةِ: The wilderness or open desert area
key_terms.الْمُصَدَّقَةُ: The ratified/confirmed one (referring to the woman's self-testimony)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for marrying a woman in the wilderness who has no guardian present?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'self-ratification' (al-muṣaddaqah 'an nafsihā), where a woman in a remote area without a male guardian (al-ghārib) can validate her own marriage proposal through testimony. The Imam confirms that her declaration of being unmarried is sufficient legal proof, reflecting the Shia juristic view that in the absence of a wali, her word carries the weight of evidence for the validity of the contract.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Muyassar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I meet the woman in the wilderness wherein there is no one. So I am saying to her, ‘Is there a husband for you?’ So she is saying, ‘No’. So I marry her’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, she is the ratified one upon herself’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Muyassir who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I may find a woman in the wilderness where she has no one and I ask her if she has a husband. She says that she does not have a husband; if I can marry her. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, you can do so; her words are accepted.’”
